lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Friday evening, Block 208. Her maths test is back.
**Kavya:** **12 out of 20**. And every mark I lost was a **minus sign**.
**Mum:** Corrections **tonight**, Kavya. Tomorrow is the **RC Family Day** at the void deck.
**Ah Boy:** Free **ice cream**! A **lucky draw**! Priya's **robot**!
**Dad:** And a **maths quiz**. First prize: a **rice cooker**. That rice cooker is **ours**.
**Kavya:** I **hate** minus signs.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about Kavya. It is about the little line in front of her wrong answers.
**Dash:** Dash. I'm the **minus sign**. **Less than zero**. Everybody **hates** me.
**Dash:** I wrote a poem. 'Roses are red. Violets are blue. I am less than zero.' It doesn't rhyme. **Nothing** works out for me.
**Ah Boy:** Kavya. Your test is **talking**.
**Dash:** Tomorrow I prove minus signs are **useful**. Or I go back to bed.
**Narrator:** Negative Vibes. Episode 1: Two Wrongs Make a Right.
**Narrator:** Saturday, 9 a.m. The RC Family Day. Auntie Rose has brought her ice-cream freezer.
**Auntie Rose:** Kavya! My freezer must be **−18 °C**. Ah Boy left the lid open. Now it's **−5 °C**!
**Dash:** **Up** the number line is **warmer**. Change = **final − start** = **−5 − (−18)**.
**Kavya:** 5 − (−1) = **6**. 5 − (−2) = **7**. The answer keeps going **up**!
**Dash:** **Subtracting a negative is adding**: a − (−b) = a + b. So −5 − (−18) = −5 + 18 = **13**.
**Ah Boy:** I know a rule! **Two negatives make a positive**! So −4 + (−6) = **10**!
**Dash:** That rule is for **×** and **÷** only. **Adding** a negative moves you **left**: −4 + (−6) = **−10**.
**Kavya:** So −7 + 4 − (−5): **4 right** to −3, then **5 more right**: **2**.
**Auntie Rose:** My freezer and a Singapore afternoon: the **difference** is **33 − (−18) = 51** degrees! Ah Boy, **close the lid**.
**Priya:** Priya. Undefeated. **Black** cards are **positive**, **red** cards are **negative**. Biggest **product** wins.
**Priya:** Black **3**, red **4**: three lots of −4. 3 × (−4) = **−12**.
**Kavya:** I've got **two reds**. (−3) × (−4) is... also −12?
**Dasha:** Hiii! **Dasha**, his twin! Watch two negatives **multiply**!
**Dash:** We make a **positive**. Ugh. I feel... **positive**.
**Dash:** **Same signs: positive. Different signs: negative.** Division as well: −12 ÷ (−3) = **4**.
**Ah Boy:** Like friends! A friend of a friend is a **friend**. An enemy of an enemy is a **friend**!
**Dash:** I don't have friends. I have a **sister**.
**Kavya:** Size first: 1 × 2 × 3 × 4 × 5 = **120**. **Five** negatives is **odd**, so **−120**. Even would be positive.
**Mr Tan:** Mr Tan. **Estimate** first: −38 × 21 ≈ −40 × 20 = **−800**. Exact: **−798**. Close!
**Priya:** **12** beats **−12**. Fine. I'm telling everyone I **let** you win.
**Dad:** Eleven a.m. The maths quiz. Team name: **Dad and the Calculators**. That rice cooker is **ours**.
**Mr Tan:** Quizmaster Tan. Question one: **√4 + 16 × 2**.
**Mum:** **6**. Obviously.
**Queenie:** Ding-dong! I'm **Queenie**, the queue machine. Nobody **cuts** my queue.
**Queenie:** Now serving: **B**rackets. Then **I**ndices: powers **and** roots. Then **D**ivision and **M**ultiplication. Then **A**ddition and **S**ubtraction.
**Queenie:** Dad went left to right: 18 × 2 = 36. Mum put **everything** under the root: √36 = 6. **Queue cutters!**
**Mr Tan:** Question two: **12 ÷ 3 × 2**.
**Mum:** **Multiplication** first! 3 × 2 = 6, and 12 ÷ 6 = **2**.
**Queenie:** **D** and **M** share **one ticket**: **left to right**. 12 ÷ 3 = 4, then 4 × 2 = **8**. **A** and **S** too.
**Mr Tan:** Question three: **20 − 3 × (5 − 7)²**.
**Kavya:** Brackets: 5 − 7 = −2. Indices: (−2)² = **4**. Multiply: 3 × 4 = 12. Subtract: 20 − 12 = **8**.
**Dad:** Last question. My calculator says **−3² = −9**. It's **broken**!
**Queenie:** The power touches only the **3**: −3² = −(3²) = **−9**. For **(−3)² = 9**, type the **brackets**.
**Mr Tan:** Results. Third place: Dad and the Calculators. Your prize: a **calculator**.
**Dad:** We **are** the calculators now.
**Priya:** Noon. My robot, the **Power-inator**: **square**, **cube**, **square root**, **cube root**. Any number.
**Ah Boy:** **7**! **Squared**, please!
**Pip:** Beep. I am **Pip**. 7² = 7 × 7 = **49**. A **square number**.
**Pip:** **Cubes** use **three** equal factors: 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = **64**. And 10³ = **1000**.
**Priya:** Reverse gear! **√49**. Easy: **7**.
**Dash:** What about **−7**? (−7) × (−7) is **also 49**. Nobody ever counts **me**.
**Pip:** Correct. 49 has **two** square roots: **±7**. The **√** sign alone means the **positive** one.
**Kavya:** So **x² = 49** gives **x = ±7**: **both** answers. Question 6. **Four marks.**
**Kavya:** And **√50**? Not a whole number. **Trap** it: 49 < 50 < 64. So √50 is between **7** and **8**. Just over 7.
**Priya:** See? Squaring **always** makes a number **bigger**.
**Ah Boy:** Can I put in **a half**?
**Priya:** **0.25**? That's **smaller**! My machine is **broken**!
**Kavya:** Half of a half is a **quarter**. Squaring a number **between 0 and 1** makes it **smaller**.
**Priya:** Then a **root** must shrink it too. **√0.25**!
**Pip:** √0.25 = **0.5**, because 0.5² = 0.25. The root is **bigger**.
**Dash:** My turn. Put **me** in. **−3**. Squared.
**Dash:** I came out **positive**. Get it **off** me.
**Kavya:** So a **negative squared** is **positive**. Now **cube** him: **−2**.
**Pip:** (−2)³ = (−2) × (−2) × (−2) = 4 × (−2) = **−8**. Three negatives: still **negative**.
**Pip:** So **∛(−8) = −2**. Every number has exactly **one** cube root.
**Dash:** Last one. The **square root** of **−9**.
**Pip:** 3² = 9. (−3)² = 9. **Nothing** squares to −9. **ERROR. NO REAL ANSWER.**
**Mr Tan:** Three zones. **Bigger than 1**: squares **grow**, roots **shrink**. **Between 0 and 1**: squares **shrink**, roots **grow**.
**Mr Tan:** **Negative**: squares **flip** to positive, cubes **stay** negative, cube roots work, square roots **don't exist**. And 0 and 1 never move.
**Priya:** Power-inator **2** comes with a **warning label**.
**Mum:** Two p.m. The folding challenge! Each fold **doubles** the layers. **Three** folds: 2 × 2 × 2 = **8** layers.
**Tiny:** That's **2³**! I'm **Tiny**, the **index**! I count how many **2s** are multiplied!
**Basil:** I am **Basil**. The **base**. I do not change.
**Dad:** **3** folds, then **4** more. So 2³ × 2⁴ = **4⁷**!
**Basil:** **The base. Does not. Change.**
**Tiny:** Three 2s, then four more 2s: **seven** 2s. 2³ × 2⁴ = **2⁷**. **Multiply: add the indices!**
**Mum:** Now **unfold** three times: 2⁷ ÷ 2³ = **2⁴**. **Divide: subtract.**
**Tiny:** **Power of a power: multiply.** (2³)⁴ = 2³ × 2³ × 2³ × 2³ = **2¹²**.
**Kavya:** And **no** folds? 2³ ÷ 2³ = 1, and the law says **2⁰**. So **2⁰ = 1**: one sheet!
**Tiny:** **MAD SPM!** **M**ultiply, **A**dd. **D**ivide, **S**ubtract. **P**ower, **M**ultiply.
**Kavya:** Letters as well: **3x² × 4x⁵ = 12x⁷**. Multiply the numbers, add the indices.
**Basil:** **Same base only.** 2³ × 5² is just 8 × 25 = **200**.
**Mum:** **42** folds of 0.1 mm paper: 0.1 × 2⁴² mm ≈ **440 000 km**. Past the **Moon**!
**Dad:** I've done **six** folds. It won't do a **seventh**.
**Mr Tan:** Four p.m. Mr Tan, photographer. Numbers have **families** too. Each fits **inside** the next.
**Ah Boy:** **Natural numbers**: the counting ones. **1, 2, 3, 4**… I'm good at those.
**Dash:** **Integers**: whole numbers, positive, negative and **zero**. I'm in this one. I **belong** somewhere.
**Kavya:** **Rational** numbers: any fraction **a/b** of integers, b ≠ 0. Like **2/5**, 0.75 = **3/4**, and 0.333… = **1/3**.
**Mum:** Every integer is rational too: −6 = −6/1. **Natural ⊂ integers ⊂ rational**. **Nesting dolls**.
**Kavya:** **Simplify first.** √16 = **4**: natural. −√9 = **−3**: integer. 12/4 = **3**: natural.
**Uncle Pi:** Hello, hello! **Uncle Pi**! **3.1415926535**…
**Mr Tan:** π is **irrational**: his decimals never **end** and never **repeat**. No fraction can make him. Same for **√2**.
**Mr Tan:** Rational and irrational together make the **real numbers**. Everybody say **cheese**!
**Narrator:** Six p.m. Back at the flat. Auntie Rose has sent home **16** pieces of kueh lapis.
**Ah Boy:** I'm **not** stopping. Half the last piece: **½**. Then **¼**. Then **⅛**.
**Kavya:** The index keeps going **down**: **2⁻¹ = ½**, **2⁻² = ¼**, **2⁻³ = ⅛**.
**Dash:** A **negative** index! Finally, a power that's one of **us**!
**Tiny:** Sorry! A negative index means **flip**, not **minus**: a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ. So 2⁻³ = 1/2³ = **⅛**. Not −8.
**Dash:** Even the **powers** won't let me be negative.
**Mum:** Powers of ten: **10⁻¹ = 0.1**, **10⁻² = 0.01**, **10⁻³ = 0.001**. And the laws still work: 2³ × 2⁻⁵ = **2⁻²**.
**Ah Boy:** So this crumb is **2⁻¹⁰**: one over **1024**. Still counts.

chapters.title: The void deck saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the Family Day would like to save you some marks.
**Queenie:** One. **×** and **÷** share a ticket: **left to right**. 12 ÷ 3 × 2 = **8**, not 2.
**Kavya:** Three. **x² = 25** has **two** answers: **x = 5** or **x = −5**. Four marks, **back**.
**Dad:** Four. Type **(−3)²** with **brackets**. Without them you get −9. Ask my calculator.
**Mum:** Five. A **fraction bar** is a bracket: (8 + 4)/(2 × 3) = 12/6 = **2**. Whole top, whole bottom, then divide.
**Auntie Rose:** Six. **−7 °C** to **5 °C** is a rise of 5 − (−7) = **12** degrees. Not 2. Ask my freezer.
**Narrator:** Negative Vibes will return.
**Kavya:** Mr Tan says **20 out of 20**. Not one sign wrong.
**Dash:** Not one minus sign lost. I'm so **proud**, I could... oh no.
**Dash:** Ugh. **Positive**.
**Narrator:** Meanwhile, at the void deck...
